topic: Skewflation: a few items in the price basket rise much faster than overall inflation

concepts.name: price basket
concepts.prereq_recalled: earlier video: the government forms a basket of commodities to measure price level

concepts.name: overall vs individual prices
concepts.prereq_recalled: basket overall price up = inflation, down = deflation

concepts.name: skewflation
concepts.prereq_recalled: we judge inflation by the basket's overall price, not single items

book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook would define skewflation in one line. This video first rebuilds inflation and deflation as moves in a basket's overall price, then opens the basket to show items moving unequally, and only then names skewflation as the case where a few items race ahead while the average looks normal. A real case and the term's origin come last. Whole first, then the parts, then the term where the parts disagree with the whole.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Go from the whole (general price level) to the parts (items in the basket), and name the new term at the point where the parts disagree with the whole.

opening.what: Names skewflation, then at once rebuilds inflation and deflation from 'general price level going up or down' on a growing tree.

moves.what: General price level of goods and services going up is inflation.
The same level going down is deflation.
Already studied: the government forms a basket of commodities consumed by all strata.
So far: basket's overall price up = inflation, down = deflation.
The basket holds hundreds of items whose prices move up and down daily, and some may even fall.
Lekin we do not watch single items; the overall basket price decides inflation or deflation.
But sometimes the overall rate is normal while particular items rise much faster.
Iska matlab: particular goods rising much faster than the overall rate of inflation.
Last seen in India in 2009 and 2010: food inflation above 20% while WPI stayed under 11%.
If we had looked only at WPI, everything would have looked normal.
Only when food prices were looked at separately did the fast rise show; this was termed skewflation.
Exam-style fact: an Indian coinage, first seen in the Economic Survey 2009-10.

examples.what: A shopping basket standing for the set of commodities the price level is measured on.
Eight coloured goods, each with an up-arrow of a different height (on screen).
examples.carries: overall price as an average of unequal moves

examples.what: 2009-10: food inflation above 20% while WPI stayed below 11%.
Had we looked only at WPI, all would have seemed normal.

closing.what: Ends on the term's origin (Economic Survey 2009-10) under a promo overlay; no recap.

narration.density: About 6 terms (general price level, inflation, deflation, basket, overall price, skewflation) plus WPI in about 150 s, about 2.5 per minute. The first 80 s are mostly review, so the new idea gets about 70 s; that suits a single-idea clip.

talmel_summary: Tree nodes pop in on or up to about 1.5 s before the voice names them, which primes the eye, and the basket, then the item arrows, then two tall arrows boxed, show skewflation without needing the text. But no visual change happens between about 100 s and 143 s: the 2009-10 case and its two numbers are told over a frozen picture, and the term's origin is told under a promo.

voice.notes: About 189 words per minute, calm and explaining. 'Basket ka overall price' is repeated many times as the anchor phrase. Numbers are read plainly ('20% se bhi zyada', '11% ke neeche'). 'Skewflation' is stressed when first named and again after 'iska matlab'. One short pause (about 0.6 s) before 'but' at 79 s marks the turn to the new idea.

game_ideas.player_does: Watches a basket of eight goods month by month with only the overall price gauge visible; can 'open the basket' (costs a turn) to see each item's arrow; each month calls it: normal, inflation, deflation or skewflation.
game_ideas.process_happens: Item arrows grow by different amounts and the overall chip shows their weighted average; in some months two items (food) race ahead while the average stays normal.
game_ideas.win: Call skewflation in the right months and name the racing items.
game_ideas.lose: Calling skewflation when every item rises together shows that this is plain inflation; watching only the gauge and missing the racing items replays the 2009-10 case (WPI calm, food above 20%).

game_ideas.player_does: Sets how much each of eight goods' price rises this year.
game_ideas.process_happens: The arrows grow to match and the overall price chip moves to their average; the tree under the basket lights inflation, deflation or neither.
game_ideas.win: Hit a target overall inflation with at least one item falling, showing items can disagree with the total.
game_ideas.lose: If two items are pushed far above the rest while the total stays on target, the screen flags skewflation instead of a pass.

notes_questions.q: Inflation, deflation aur skewflation: teeno ka fark ek table mein.
Price level napne ke liye 'basket' kya hai, aur usme kiske istemal ki cheezein hoti hain?
2009-10 mein skewflation kaise dikha? Food inflation aur WPI ki tulna kijiye.
Sirf WPI dekhte to kya chhoot jaata?
Skewflation shabd pehli baar kahan aur kab aaya?

checks_learned: A real case with two numbers to compare (above 20% vs below 11%) needs a picture of the comparison (for example two bars); flag a canvas that stays unchanged for more than about 30 s while a case is told.
When the voice says some items fall, at least one item on screen must show a down arrow.
No promo overlay may cover the canvas while a teaching sentence is being spoken.
Term nodes that pop in about 0.5-1.5 s before the spoken term work well; flag nodes more than 3 s early, or after the word.
A definition box that repeats the voice word for word should be replaced by the visual it describes or cut.

teaching_best.why: One arrow per item, with height = size of the price rise, makes 'the overall price is an average of unequal moves' visible.
The 'but sometimes' contrast builds the new term out of the old one: average normal, a few items racing.
The what-if (only WPI watched) shows why the term was needed at all.

teaching_weak.why: The 2009-10 case and its numbers are only spoken; the picture stays frozen for about 40 s.
The first ~27 s are a thin-text tree that only re-teaches inflation and deflation.
The exam fact is told under a promo overlay, and there is no recap.
